episode.title: Consolidate dynamic-tool persistence onto rollout session metadata while retaining schema compatibility
episode.before: At parent commit 0db49a7e6ae8fd459dd8d8d404086c748b9118a1, thread-start dynamic tools had two persistence paths. Rollout SessionMeta stored them, while SQLite also copied them into thread_dynamic_tools through incremental rollout application, rollout backfill/reconciliation, and thread-metadata synchronization. When a resumed or forked session supplied no tools directly, session initialization queried SQLite first and only then fell back to rollout history.
episode.after: At commit 304d15cab0b1c5f23925e5a3b94c39db3483fc3d, rollout session metadata is the sole active persistence and restoration path for thread-start dynamic tools. Session initialization obtains missing tools directly from conversation history even when SQLite is enabled; SQLite reads, writes, backfill/reconciliation, and metadata-patch propagation for dynamic tools are removed. The existing thread_dynamic_tools table and migrations remain intact for older-binary compatibility.
episode.diff: The change modifies nine Rust files with 101 insertions and 260 deletions. It simplifies session initialization from a database-first/fallback lookup to conversation_history.get_dynamic_tools(), deletes dynamic-tool database APIs and extraction logic, removes dynamic_tools from ThreadMetadataPatch and synchronization paths, removes the backfill assertion that tools are copied into SQLite, and adds an SQLite-enabled resume integration test that starts a thread with a tool, resumes from its rollout, and verifies the restored tool name, description, and input schema in the next request.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit identifies rollout SessionMeta as the existing restoration source, calls SQLite storage redundant, and states that SQLite dynamic-tool reads, writes, backfill, and metadata-patch plumbing are removed.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller 304d15cab0b1c5f23925e5a3b94c39db3483fc3d; commit message sections Why and What changed

evidence_units.claim: In the parent state, missing thread-start tools for resumed or forked histories were looked up from the local SQLite state runtime first and then obtained from conversation history only as a fallback.
evidence_units.source: git show 304d15cab0b1c5f23925e5a3b94c39db3483fc3d^:codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs, session initialization around the removed persisted_tools block

evidence_units.claim: After the change, when explicit dynamic_tools are empty, session initialization directly uses conversation_history.get_dynamic_tools().unwrap_or_default(), with no SQLite lookup.
evidence_units.source: git show 304d15cab0b1c5f23925e5a3b94c39db3483fc3d:codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs, session initialization comment and dynamic_tools assignment

evidence_units.claim: The state runtime no longer exposes get_dynamic_tools or persist_dynamic_tools, no longer extracts tools from rollout items during incremental application, and no longer writes rows to thread_dynamic_tools.
Rollout backfill and reconciliation stop reading SessionMeta solely to copy dynamic tools into SQLite, and the rollout state wrapper functions for SQLite tool reads and writes are removed.
Dynamic tools are removed from ThreadMetadataPatch, patch merging and emptiness checks, initial metadata observations, rollout-item observations, and local metadata update application.
The existing rollout-backfill test no longer seeds dynamic tools in SessionMeta or polls SQLite for a copied value, while retaining assertions for the metadata that backfill still owns.

The added integration test enables SQLite, starts a thread with a dynamic tool, completes a turn, resumes from the rollout path, submits another turn, and verifies that the resumed request includes the tool with its original name, description, and input schema.
The commit deliberately leaves the thread_dynamic_tools table and its migrations present but unused so older binaries can still open and use databases migrated by newer binaries.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller 304d15cab0b1c5f23925e5a3b94c39db3483fc3d; Compatibility section, corroborated by codex-rs/state/migrations/0004_thread_dynamic_tools.sql, 0019_thread_dynamic_tools_defer_loading.sql, and 0026_thread_dynamic_tools_namespace.sql remaining in the commit tree

evidence_units.claim: The implementation changes nine files across session initialization, rollout/state persistence, thread metadata synchronization, and integration tests, totaling 101 insertions and 260 deletions.

The commit records package-level tests for state, rollout, and thread-store plus the focused SQLite-enabled resume integration test as its verification commands; execution results are not present in the supplied bundle.
The supplied GitHub evidence bundle links issue/PR 24819 to the pinned implementation commit and classifies it as a training candidate with an implementation and test change.

candidate_atomics.name: select-authoritative-persisted-state-source
candidate_atomics.title: Restore immutable session configuration from its authoritative history record
candidate_atomics.description: Route restoration of thread-start configuration through the persisted session history that already defines and stores it, instead of preferring a secondary database replica.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure resumed or forked sessions recover their original thread-start tools without depending on a redundant cache or replica.
semantic_action.module_role: session initialization and history restoration boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: The caller supplies no new dynamic tools, and a resumed or forked conversation history may contain the tools recorded at thread creation; a secondary database lookup currently precedes that history.
semantic_action.post_state: Explicit caller-supplied tools remain authoritative when present; otherwise the session uses tools from persisted conversation history or an empty list when history has none.
semantic_action.validation: Resume a persisted thread while SQLite is enabled and assert that the next outbound request contains the rollout-defined tool with its original contract.

candidate_atomics.name: remove-redundant-state-replication-path
candidate_atomics.title: Remove writes, reads, and synchronization for the redundant state replica
candidate_atomics.description: Delete the full active lifecycle of a duplicated persisted field after its authoritative source and restoration path are established.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent duplicated persistent state from developing inconsistent ownership or restoration behavior.
semantic_action.module_role: secondary state-store persistence and metadata synchronization layers
semantic_action.pre_state: The same immutable thread-start tools are copied from rollout metadata into SQLite through incremental ingestion, backfill, reconciliation, and metadata patches, and can be read back during session initialization.
semantic_action.post_state: No runtime path reads, writes, backfills, reconciles, or metadata-patches dynamic tools through the secondary store; unrelated thread metadata continues to use those mechanisms.
semantic_action.validation: Compile and test the affected state, rollout, and thread-store packages, and confirm the backfill integration test still validates its remaining metadata responsibilities without expecting a tool replica.
parameters: metadata patch field and merge logic

candidate_atomics.name: retain-dormant-schema-for-compatibility
candidate_atomics.title: Retain the unused persisted schema for mixed-version compatibility
candidate_atomics.description: Stop using a redundant table at runtime without dropping it when older binaries may still require that schema against databases migrated by newer versions.

semantic_action.intent: Simplify current persistence ownership without making newer database files unreadable or unusable by supported older binaries.
semantic_action.module_role: persistent schema evolution and version-compatibility boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: The secondary table is no longer needed by the new runtime, but older binaries may still query or write it when opening the same migrated database.
semantic_action.post_state: The new runtime leaves the table unused while its schema and migrations remain available for mixed-version operation.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the resulting migration set to confirm the table-creating and column-altering migrations remain, and include compatibility coverage where the project has an older-binary database test harness.

candidate_atomics.name: verify-authoritative-resume-restoration
candidate_atomics.title: Verify restoration through the real resume request boundary
candidate_atomics.description: Exercise creation, persistence, resume, and outbound serialization so the test proves the canonical history source restores the complete runtime contract while the secondary store is enabled.

semantic_action.intent: Demonstrate that removing the replica does not lose persisted configuration during an actual resumed interaction.
semantic_action.pre_state: A thread has been started with a non-default dynamic tool, persisted to rollout history, and is resumed without resupplying that tool while the secondary database feature is enabled.
semantic_action.post_state: The first request after resume contains the original tool name, description, and parameter schema.
semantic_action.validation: Assert two requests occurred and inspect the resumed request's tools array for exact semantic fields from the original specification.

candidate_workflows.name: consolidate-duplicated-persistent-state-owner
candidate_workflows.title: Consolidate duplicated persistent state without breaking restoration or older schemas
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for replacing two active persistence paths with one authoritative history source, removing the redundant replica end to end, preserving compatibility-sensitive schema, and proving behavior at the resume boundary.

workflow_graph.goal: Make one persisted history record authoritative for immutable session configuration, eliminate the secondary runtime replica, and retain any schema required for mixed-version compatibility while preserving resume behavior.
when_to_use: The same immutable or thread-start state is persisted in both an authoritative event/history record and a secondary database representation.
Resume or fork behavior can reconstruct the state from the authoritative record.
The duplicated path spans reads, writes, ingestion/backfill, reconciliation, or metadata synchronization and creates competing ownership.
A legacy schema may still be referenced by older supported binaries.
anti_goals: Do not change the dynamic-tool contract, ordering, description, input schema, namespace semantics, or caller override precedence.
Do not remove unrelated thread metadata persistence or backfill responsibilities.
Do not drop a legacy table merely because the current runtime stops using it.
Do not treat the secondary database as the new source of truth when the durable session record already owns the state.
not_applicable_when: The secondary store is the only durable source available during restoration.
The duplicated values are mutable independently and require reconciliation rather than single ownership.
Mixed-version compatibility is explicitly unsupported and schema removal has a separate validated migration plan.
No integration boundary can demonstrate that restored state reaches its runtime consumer.
inputs: The authoritative persisted record and its field semantics
All secondary-store read and write call sites
Backfill, reconciliation, and metadata-patch propagation paths
Legacy schema and supported-version compatibility policy
An integration-test fixture that captures the first post-resume consumer request
workflow_graph.entry_state: One logical field has two active persistence paths: the durable session history contains it, SQLite also stores and serves a copy, and restoration prefers the SQLite copy before falling back to history.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The durable history is the sole active owner and restoration source, all runtime replication plumbing for the field is removed, the compatibility-sensitive legacy schema remains available, and an integration test proves the full field contract survives resume with the secondary-store feature enabled.

steps.condition: Use when the durable history record is available to resumed or forked initialization and already contains the immutable thread-start value.
steps.validation: Compare parent and resulting initialization paths and confirm explicit inputs still win while missing inputs come directly from history.

steps.condition: Proceed only after the authoritative restoration path is established; remove field-specific reads, writes, extraction, backfill, reconciliation, and metadata-patch propagation without disturbing unrelated metadata.
steps.validation: Affected packages compile and their tests pass; repository inspection finds no active secondary-store API or synchronization call site for the field.

steps.condition: Required when supported older binaries can open databases migrated by the newer binary and still reference the legacy table.
steps.validation: The table-creating and follow-up migrations remain in the resulting tree even though current runtime call sites are absent.

steps.condition: Run with the secondary persistence feature enabled so the test detects accidental dependence on or interference from that path.
steps.validation: A thread created with a tool is resumed from its rollout, and the next request contains the original name, description, and parameter schema.

validation_ladder: Static inspection: verify the runtime restoration branch reads the authoritative history record and preserves explicit-input precedence.
Call-site inspection: verify field-specific secondary-store APIs, ingestion, backfill, reconciliation, and metadata-patch propagation are absent.
Component validation: run the state, rollout, and thread-store package tests reported by the commit.
Behavioral integration: create and resume a thread with the secondary database enabled, then inspect the first resumed request for the complete restored field contract.
Compatibility validation: confirm legacy schema migrations remain; execute mixed-version database tests if such a harness is available.
stop_conditions: Stop if the authoritative record does not contain the field for all supported resume or fork cases.
Stop if any runtime consumer still depends exclusively on the secondary representation.
Stop before dropping the legacy schema unless supported-version policy and migration tests explicitly authorize it.
Stop if the integration test cannot distinguish restoration from explicit resupply or fixture defaults.
Stop if removing the field-specific plumbing also removes unrelated metadata persistence behavior.
unresolved_or_deferred: The supplied evidence does not include executed test logs; verification commands are reported by the commit but were not rerun in the deletion-filled working tree.
The commit states that resumed and forked sessions are restored from rollout metadata, but the added integration test directly covers resume only.
No executable mixed-version older-binary compatibility test is shown; schema retention is supported by the commit rationale and retained migration files.

unresolved_questions: The checkout working tree contains broad pre-existing staged deletions unrelated to the pinned change, so evidence was obtained with read-only git object inspection rather than by running the repository tests.
GitHub issue body, comments, reviews, timeline, and status-check results are unavailable in the supplied bundle.
Whether fork restoration has dedicated coverage elsewhere was not established by the changed test; the new regression test proves only the resumed-session path.
Actual execution outcomes for the verification commands are not available; only the commit's declared verification commands are evidenced.
